slides.title: China’s UBTech unveils humanoid robot companion with lifelike skin and ‘emotional AI’
slides.highlight: UBTech has introduced a humanoid robot companion featuring lifelike skin and emotional AI, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Chinese Tech Firm Unveils Robot Companion
slides.highlight: The introduction of a robot companion highlights ongoing debates regarding the impact of social robots on real-life relationships, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Uncovering Salience-Driven Dynamics in Consumer Confidence with Generative Social Simulation
slides.tldr: GENERATIVE SOCIAL SIMULATION FOR CONSUMER CONFIDENCE
slides.highlight: This research introduces ConsumerSim, a generative framework that reconstructs Consumer Confidence Index dynamics using synthetic populations and behavioral responses, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: ConsumerSim reconstructs Consumer Confidence Index dynamics as a salience-driven response process between heterogeneous agents and environments.
card.key_idea: A generative framework using microdata-calibrated synthetic populations, situational signal fields, and behavioral inertia alignment to simulate how diverse households respond to salient economic shocks.
card.evaluation: Evaluated against U.S., EU27, and Japan CCI series; outperformed 14 baselines in MAE/RMSE and improved short-horizon housing activity predictions.
card.limitation: Relies on external signal quality, uses generative agents as imperfect cognitive proxies, and lacks full local population substrates for non-U.S. regions.

slides.title: Will Scaling Improve Social Simulation with LLMs?
slides.tldr: SCALING LAWS IN LLM SOCIAL SIMULATION
slides.highlight: This research examines how compute scale affects the fidelity of LLM-based social simulations, providing insights for the agent models used in MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Scaling compute generally improves LLM social simulation, but fails for specific cognitive biases and underrepresented populations.
card.key_idea: The authors used compute-scaling laws (85 Qwen3 models) and observational laws (35 open-weight models) to analyze opinion, behavior, and longitudinal simulations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using World Values Survey, Psych-101, and ACL datasets across 120+ models; results show strong log-linear scaling for most tasks.
card.limitation: Scaling fails to improve calibration for human cognitive biases (e.g., risk aversion) and tasks with high population heterogeneity.

slides.title: TurnNat: Automatic Evaluation of Turn-Taking Naturalness in Dyadic Spoken Dialogue
slides.highlight: TurnNat provides a likelihood-based framework to automatically evaluate turn-taking naturalness in spoken dialogue, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: TurnNat provides a unified likelihood-based framework to automatically evaluate turn-taking naturalness in dyadic spoken dialogues.
card.key_idea: It uses a causal model to predict future voice-activity states; naturalness is measured by aggregating negative log-likelihoods over extracted turn-taking boundary units (TBUs).
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a human-validated perturbation benchmark using C-index and pairwise accuracy. DualTurn-based models achieved up to 88.0% matched-pair accuracy.
card.limitation: Focuses only on voice activity, potentially missing naturalness factors related to lexical content, discourse intent, or system-side ASR errors.

slides.title: REPAIR-Bench: A Benchmark for Robot Error Perception And Interaction Recovery
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR ROBOT FAILURE PERCEPTION AND RECOVERY
slides.highlight: This work introduces REPAIR-Bench to evaluate how users perceive robot failures and predict preferred recovery strategies, supporting the development of trustworthy human-robot interaction for RwB.

card.one_liner: REPAIR-Bench is a multimodal benchmark for detecting, classifying, and predicting recovery strategies for robot failures.
card.key_idea: It uses Hierarchical Recurrent Neural Networks (HRNN) for temporal failure detection/classification and QLoRA-tuned Small Language Models (Mistral-7B, Gemma-9B) for predicting user-preferred recovery strategies.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 184 interaction trials using F1-score, Hit@k, and localization error; HRNN achieved 0.80 strict F1 for detection.
card.limitation: Small sample size (184 trials) for recovery prediction and reliance on a predefined set of recovery strategies.

slides.title: Understanding LLM Intervention Explanations in Multi-Party Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: LLM INTERVENTION EXPLANATIONS IN MULTI-PARTY HRI
slides.highlight: This research examines how LLM-based orchestrators justify decisions to intervene in group conversations involving humans and robots. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: LLM-driven robots in multi-party settings act primarily as facilitators, prioritizing agreement and participation balance.
card.key_idea: An LLM orchestrator manages two robots (mover/opposer roles), generating textual explanations for its real-time decisions to intervene in human group negotiations.
card.evaluation: Thematic analysis of 610 explanations from 24 groups (66 students) using a between-subjects study with homogeneous and heterogeneous role configurations.
card.limitation: Did not evaluate if explanations improved user transparency or link robot behaviors to objective task success rates.

slides.title: Who Plays Which Role When? Communication Role Dynamics for Peer Recognition and Team Performance Prediction
slides.tldr: COMMUNICATION ROLE DYNAMICS FOR TEAM PERFORMANCE
slides.highlight: This work operationalizes a taxonomy of communication roles to characterize team dynamics and predict performance, contributing to HyECHO's focus on modeling hybrid team states and engagement.

card.one_liner: Theory-grounded communication roles predicted by LLMs improve the prediction of peer recognition and team performance.
card.key_idea: Operationalized an eight-role taxonomy using LLMs to annotate longitudinal Slack data, analyzing role dynamics and using these features to predict individual and team success.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on student Slack messages and DeliData dataset using ROC-AUC; outperformed lexical, conversational, and zero-shot LLM baselines.
card.limitation: Primary data from one CS course; potential selection bias from consenting students and reliance on proprietary LLM prompting.

slides.title: LLM-Powered Interactive Robotic Action Synthesis from Multimodal Speech, Gestures, and Music
slides.highlight: This framework uses LLMs to synthesize robotic actions from speech, gestures, and music, supporting the RwB goal of creating fluid and context-aware human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: An LLM-powered framework synthesizing quadruped robot actions from combined speech, hand gestures, and music beats.
card.key_idea: Integrates Whisper (speech), gesture recognition, and beat detection into structured prompts for a small LLM (Qwen3:0.6b) to map inputs to a pre-vetted robot action space.
card.evaluation: Validated via preliminary experiments on a Unitree Go2 quadruped robot, demonstrating successful execution of a handstand triggered by a gesture and beat.
card.limitation: Limited by a predefined action space and the need for further optimization of real-time LLM inference pipelines.

slides.title: Vision-Language Models for Deployable Social Robot Navigation: Bridging Semantic Reasoning and Low-Level Control
slides.highlight: This survey explores integrating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) with low-level control to enable socially compliant navigation. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A survey on integrating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) into socially compliant robot navigation systems.
card.key_idea: Proposes a hierarchical framework coupling high-level VLM semantic reasoning with low-level planning via a bridging module that translates reasoning into executable costs and constraints.
card.evaluation: Reviews existing SRN datasets and platforms; notes a lack of standardized evaluation protocols for deployment-oriented performance.
card.limitation: High computational cost and inference latency of VLMs hinder real-time deployment on resource-constrained mobile robots.

slides.title: Metric Aggregation Divergence: A Hidden Validity Threat in Agent-Based Policy Optimization and a Contractual Remedy
slides.tldr: REMEDY FOR METRIC AGGREGATION DIVERGENCE IN ABM+MOEA
slides.highlight: This research identifies metric aggregation divergence in agent-based models coupled with multi-objective evolutionary algorithms and proposes a 'metric contract' to ensure consistency. This is relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Metric Aggregation Divergence (MAD) silently alters optimal policy recommendations when pipeline stages independently re-implement outcome metrics.
card.key_idea: MAD occurs in ABM+MOEA pipelines when different stages use incommensurable aggregators. The authors propose a 'metric contract'—a single shared callable enforced across all pipeline stages.
card.evaluation: Tested via controlled experiments, a replication of EpidemiOptim (64.2% champion disagreement), and a Lake Problem workflow audit. Results show high rank-reversal rates.
card.limitation: Empirical validation is limited to four ABM types across two domains; generalizability to other domains like transportation or energy remains open.

slides.title: SenseWalk: Agent-Based Semantic Trajectory Simulation Powered by Large Language Models in Zoned Environments
slides.highlight: SenseWalk uses LLM-powered agents and the social force model to simulate human movement patterns and semantic trajectories, aligning with MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: SenseWalk is an interactive system for simulating physically plausible and semantically coherent human trajectories in zoned environments.
card.key_idea: A hybrid workflow combining LLM-powered agents for high-level semantic planning and the social force model for low-level physical movement constraints.
card.evaluation: Quantitative experiments across four real-world venue models (CES, Shibuya PARCO, National Gallery, CIIE) using physical and semantic loss metrics.

slides.title: SICAGE: Speaker-Independent Culture-Aware Gesture Generation using TED4C-L Dataset
slides.highlight: SICAGE introduces a framework for generating culturally appropriate gestures by learning speaker-independent cultural representations from audio and text. This supports HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and understanding group norms in human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: SICAGE generates culture-aware co-speech gestures using speaker-independent embeddings to avoid confounding individual styles with culture.
card.key_idea: A modular framework using Fishr regularization or adversarial learning to extract speaker-invariant cultural embeddings from audio/text, conditioning a real-time diffusion-based generator called ALaDiT.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the new TED4C-L dataset (106h, 4 cultures) using FGD, SRGR, BAS, and a user study; ALaDiT-FI performed best.
card.limitation: The motion-based cultural classifier achieved only 45% accuracy, highlighting substantial intra-cultural variability that challenges the generation task.

slides.title: From Technical Metrics to User Perception: A User Study of a Multimodal Human-Robot Interaction System for Object Detection and Grasping
slides.tldr: USER PERCEPTION OF MULTIMODAL HRI IMPROVEMENTS
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that technical gains in object-grasping success rates are perceptible to users, supporting the need for user-centered evidence in HRI. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A user study confirms that a 15% technical success gain in a robot grasping system is perceptible.
card.key_idea: Compared a baseline (Florence-2, LLaMA 3.1) against an improved configuration (Grounding DINO + SAM, Qwen 3.5 9B) using a within-subject study on tabletop object-grasping tasks.
card.evaluation: 24 participants rated speed, reliability, and competence via 7-point Likert scales. Results showed significant improvements (p < 0.001) and a 70.83% user preference.
card.limitation: Despite improvements, reliability ratings remained near the scale midpoint, indicating the system is not yet fully dependable for real-world deployment.
